sources.citation: Cooper, Audrey C. 2011 (figshare release 2023). Overcoming the 'backward' body: How state institutions, language, and embodiment shape deaf education in contemporary southern Viet Nam. PhD dissertation (Anthropology), American University, Washington DC. 456 pp. UMI 3452637. doi:10.57912/23880852
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Anthropology thesis on deaf education; full text (scanned layer) a full-text search for stress/accent/prosod/rhythm/phonolog: no statement on stress or prominence. Only sign-structure remark (diss. p. ~252, the text layer): signs 'vary according to handshape, palm orientation, location, movement, non-manual signal, and other parameters.' Bibliography lists the Dong Nai HCMCSL learner's book Woodward, Nguyen Thi Hoa et al. 2007 'Ngon ngu ki hieu Tp. Ho Chi Minh, Sach hoc vien 2, Trinh do 1' and Woodward, Nguyen & Nguyen 2004 Deaf Worlds 20(3): 232-63.

sources.citation: Woodward, James & Nguyen Thi Hoa. 2011. Teaching sign language and Deaf Studies at university level to hearing people in Viet Nam. Japanese Journal of Sign Language Studies 20: 5-10. doi:10.7877/jasl.20.5
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress. Program-history paper: names HCMCSL, Ha Noi SL and Hai Phong SL as three related sign languages sharing 54-58% of basic core vocabulary (p. 6) and reports that Deaf teachers at Dong Nai prepared '4 sign language handbooks and 4 companion dictionaries' for HCMCSL (p. 8).

sources.citation: Woodward, James; Nguyen Thi Hoa; Nguyen Dinh Mong Giang; Le Thi Thu Huong; Luu Ngoc Tu; Ho Thu Van. 2015. Ho Chi Minh City Sign Language. In Jepsen, De Clerck, Lutalo-Kiingi & McGregor (eds.), Sign Languages of the World: A Comparative Handbook, 391-408 (Glottolog: 401-418). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
